blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Ratios become useful the moment you compare them. One profit margin on its own is just a number. Five quarters of profit margin side by side is a story. A current ratio of 1.2 is a number; a current ratio falling from 2.0 to 1.2 over a year is an alarm.

At the intermediate level, ratios are used to trigger conversations, not to prove points. When inventory turnover slows, the conversation is with operations. When receivables days grow, the conversation is with sales. When the cash conversion cycle widens, the conversation is with the whole leadership team.

Ratios are only powerful in context. Use them to open the right conversations, not to close them.

items.q: According to the text, when does a ratio become useful?
options: The moment you compare it with others
When it is reported to the board
Only when it reaches a target
As soon as it is calculated
items.why: "Ratios become useful the moment you compare them." — o valor está na comparação.

items.q: A current ratio falling from 2.0 to 1.2 over a year is described as…
options: a story with a happy ending
items.why: "a current ratio falling from 2.0 to 1.2 over a year is an alarm."

items.q: When receivables days grow, who is the conversation with?
items.why: "When receivables days grow, the conversation is with sales."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A slowing inventory turnover deserves a talk with operations.
Trends across quarters tell a clearer story than one figure.
Ratios should open conversations rather than end them.
A single ratio, on its own, proves that a decision is right.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que índices servem para disparar conversas, "not to prove points" — um número sozinho não prova nada.

items.q: The phrase "use them to open the right conversations, not to close them" suggests that…
options: ratios are only for the finance team
conversations waste time that ratios could save
ratios are a starting point, not a final verdict
ratios should end debate and settle decisions
items.why: Inferência: os índices apontam para o próximo diálogo; não fecham a discussão sozinhos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry explicando a um novo sócio de negócios como um índice em queda vira uma conversa entre times. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before I hand you the full report, let me show you why this one line worries me. Look at the current ratio across the last three quarters: 2.0, then 1.6, then 1.2. Any single number would look fine on its own. It's the slide that matters.

Now, I'm not saying the company is in trouble. A ratio of 1.2 is still above one. But the direction is the alarm here, not the level. When something drops that steadily for three quarters, it rarely fixes itself.

Here's how I read it. If I look next to it, inventory turnover has slowed and receivables days have grown. That tells me cash is getting stuck — first in the warehouse, then in unpaid invoices. The cash conversion cycle is widening.

And that's exactly why I don't want to email this to operations and finance separately. This isn't a finance problem or an ops problem. It's a conversation they need to have in the same room. My job today is simply to open that conversation, not to close it with a verdict. Once they see the trend side by side, they'll know who needs to act.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What are the three current-ratio figures Harry points to?
items.why: "2.0, then 1.6, then 1.2" — uma queda ao longo de três trimestres.

items.q: According to Harry, what is the real alarm?
options: That the ratio is below one
items.why: "the direction is the alarm here, not the level."

items.q: What does Harry infer from slower inventory turnover and growing receivables days?
options: Cash is getting stuck — in the warehouse, then in unpaid invoices
The current ratio will recover on its own
items.why: "cash is getting stuck — first in the warehouse, then in unpaid invoices."

items.q: Why does Harry NOT want to email operations and finance separately?
options: Because email is against company policy
Because the issue needs both teams talking in the same room
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que não é problema só de finanças ou só de operações — precisam conversar juntos.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's approach?
options: He downplays the numbers to avoid worry
He delivers a final verdict and assigns blame
He raises a trend to start the right conversation, not to end it
He refuses to interpret the data at all
items.why: Inferência: "open that conversation, not to close it with a verdict" — ele provoca o diálogo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The current ratio dropped below one, so the company may struggle to pay short-term bills." The current ratio measures…
options: the number of employees per manager
the ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets
items.why: Current ratio (liquidez corrente) mede a capacidade de pagar obrigações de curto prazo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A single bad quarter can ___ a full review of the supply chain."
items.why: Trigger = disparar/desencadear: um trimestre ruim dispara a revisão.

items.q: "When inventory turnover slows, goods sit on the shelf for longer." Inventory turnover refers to…
options: how fast stock is sold and replaced
the total value of the warehouse
items.why: Inventory turnover = giro de estoque: com que velocidade o estoque é vendido e reposto.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Customers are paying later, so our ___ have grown from 30 to 55."
items.why: Receivables days = dias de recebíveis: quanto tempo, em média, os clientes levam para pagar.

items.q: "The cash conversion cycle is widening." This cycle measures…
options: how long cash is tied up before it comes back as cash
the exchange rate on foreign sales
the interest rate charged by the bank
items.why: Cash conversion cycle = ciclo de conversão de caixa: o tempo entre pagar fornecedores e receber dos clientes.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem quando se discutem números e decisões. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's not read too much into a single quarter." To read too much into something means to…
options: share it with too many people
give it more importance than it deserves
items.why: Read too much into = tirar conclusões exageradas de algo pequeno.

items.q: "These small changes won't move the needle on our cash position." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The trend is flagging up a problem in receivables." To flag up means to…
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar a atenção para algo que merece ser visto.

items.q: "Before we act, let's drill down into the inventory numbers." To drill down into means to…
items.why: Drill down into = descer aos detalhes, analisar a fundo.

items.q: "Once ops and finance get on the same page, they can fix this." To get on the same page means to…
items.why: Get on the same page = alinhar-se, chegar a um entendimento comum.
